wages.text: He supports raising the minimum wage, indexing it to inflation, and strengthening workers’ union rights.
wages.quote: Workers deserve a wage that rises with inflation each year, so no one has to struggle to survive.

debt.text: His campaign says Medicare and Medicaid should be protected from federal cuts.
debt.quote: We must protect Medicare and Medicaid so everyone can get care when they need it, without worrying about losing coverage or facing impossible bills.

abortion.text: In a campaign email, he said women should make decisions about their own bodies without government interference in medical exam rooms.
abortion.quote: That women can decide what to do with their own bodies, and government should stay the hell out of our exam rooms.

health.text: His campaign supports Medicare for All to provide universal health coverage.
health.quote: Medicare for All ensures everyone can see a doctor, get medicine, and stay healthy without going into debt or skipping care.

voting.text: He supports automatic voter registration and national standards to protect voting rights.
voting.quote: We support national standards to end partisan gerrymandering and protect voting rights. That means fair maps, automatic registration, and restored protections under the Voting Rights Act.

wages.text: He calls for increasing the minimum wage and proposes a $50,000 annual salary floor for K–12 educators.
wages.quote: I propose a national minimum salary of $50,000 per year for all K through 12 educators, and that it is increased each year by the increase in the consumer price index (CPI).

trade.text: He calls for abolishing tariffs, including food tariffs, which he says raise consumer costs.
trade.quote: All tariffs on food need to be abolished because they have increased food costs for all consumers.

debt.text: He says he wants to reduce the national debt while also pledging to save Social Security.
debt.quote: Laser focused on strengthening the middle class while reducing the national debt and maintaining America's role as leader of the free world.

housing.text: He says the country needs more housing and proposes a program to help people buy first homes.
housing.quote: There is an urgent need for more housing in the U.S. and a need for an increased percentage of home ownership and a decrease in the average age of the first-time home buyer.

immigration.text: He calls for ending chain migration, defunding sanctuary cities, and limiting immigration to government-approved applicants with needed skills, with an exception for spouses and children.
immigration.quote: End chain migration - it may be nice for a family, but it is a bad immigration option for a country

guns.text: He said gun violence is more about social attitudes and behavior than gun laws, emphasizing citizenship education.
guns.quote: The issue here is social attitudes and behavior, much more than it is gun laws. Our education system needs to focus more on what it means to be a responsible citizen.

abortion.text: He says he opposes abortion and supports legal protection for human life from conception.
abortion.quote: Human life deserves legal protection from conception until natural death.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He supports excluding biological males from women’s sports and spaces.
gender.quote: Biological males should not be allowed to participate in women's sports or occupy biological women's spaces whether it be bathrooms, locker rooms, sorority houses, women's shelters, or prison.

health.text: He favors private insurance but also supports a government plan for people who cannot obtain private coverage.
health.quote: I believe private insurance is the best system but there are some people who could not obtain private insurance and government should have a plan for these people.

energy.text: He says lowering fuel costs would reduce food prices because transportation is a significant product cost.
energy.quote: Lowering fuel costs would also help decrease food costs as transportation costs account for a significant part of the total cost of all products.

voting.text: He opposes voting without photo identification and says elections should require ID.
voting.quote: It's required for so many things and should be for elections.

tax.text: On his official fiscal policy page, Johnson called for permanent tax reductions and pro-growth tax reforms.
tax.quote: pursue continued pro-growth tax reforms and permanent tax reductions

wages.text: Johnson voted against the 2019 Raise the Wage Act.
wages.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Raise the Wage Act Vote Type: Recorded Vote

trade.text: He supported using tariffs to rebalance trade and protect U.S. workers and businesses.
trade.quote: So tariffs are one tool among many that he's using to try to do a rebalancing there. He's trying to rebalance trade and restore a level playing field for American workers and businesses.

debt.text: Johnson’s official fiscal policy page calls for bringing spending under control, balancing the budget and modernizing entitlement programs.
debt.quote: Congress has a moral and constitutional duty to resolve the crisis, bring spending under control, balance the federal budget, reform and modernize entitlement programs

schools.text: He supported a federal tax-credit scholarship program for alternatives to public schools.
schools.quote: Supports School Choice: creates the first-ever federal tax credit scholarship program for K–12 students and students with special needs to access alternatives to public schools with direct financial support.

safety.text: He joined an effort seeking additional funding for Louisiana law-enforcement officers after flooding.
safety.quote: Now, we must ensure they have the resources needed to continue their service.

immigration.text: Johnson supported funding border enforcement and deportations, and said the bill would provide resources to detain and deport undocumented immigrants.
immigration.quote: provide federal law enforcement with the resources necessary to permanently fortify our borders against foreign invaders and detain and deport the millions of illegals

guns.text: Johnson voted for the Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2017.
guns.quote: Vote Question: On Passage Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2017 Vote Type: Recorded Vote

abortion.text: Johnson voted for and co-sponsored a bill to prohibit most abortions after 20 weeks of pregnancy and said he would continue that effort.
abortion.quote: I will continue this fight while in Congress.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: He supported legislation requiring federally funded schools to keep biological males out of women’s sports.
gender.quote: requiring all schools receiving federal funding to uphold the original meaning of Title IX and to keep biological men out of women's sports.

health.text: He promoted a health-care plan based on free-market options and competition rather than expanded public coverage.
health.quote: There’s ways to do that that are free market-based and introduce competition and help to drive the cost down.

energy.text: He supported expanding domestic energy production and rolling back regulations he described as raising energy costs.
energy.quote: we need reliable, affordable, abundant energy.

voting.text: He supported requiring proof of citizenship for registration and photo identification to vote in federal elections.
voting.quote: The SAVE America Act ensures, as you know, that voters have proof of citizenship to register to vote, and they show a valid ID when they turn up to vote at the ballot box.

debt.text: Nichols said rising national debt motivated him to run and recalled that the federal budget had been balanced during his lifetime.
debt.quote: Well kind of what got me motivated is our debt just keeps going higher and home in Yes, sir, And you hear a lot of people say that it's no use to fight at mine. But you know, I do remember our budget being balanced under President Clinton.
